IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging: GPU pool exhaustion detected in us-west1. HPA custom metrics delayed — autoscaler not responding. Queue growth observed on ml-inference-queue. Paging on-call.
Sam L.: on it. seeing queue depth spike from ~200 -> 1800 over last 8m. Worker pods are maxed, some pods OOM/killed earlier. Rolling 429s from gateway.
Anya P.: confirm customers hitting throttles? any high-priority affected?
Sam L.: yes, ~12% of production requests got 429/503 in last 10m. Priority routing shows majority are low-priority batch, but a few user-facing endpoints degraded (webchat).
Jin K.: kubectl HPA check: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` returns:
```
NAME             REFERENCE             TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-hpa    Deployment/inference  0(100m)    3         50        3          12d
```
Targets stuck at 0 because custom metric api call timing out.
Maya R.: Prometheus adapter logs show repeated 504s to Prometheus and backlog on scrape queue. `prom-adapter` CPU spikes.
Priya S.: metrics-server looks healthy but prom-adapter -> apiserver -> HPA path failing. Could be adapter auth or large cardinality making queries expensive.
Sam L.: immediate mitigation plan: 1) manually scale inference deployment to 20 replicas, 2) add emergency node pool (if available), 3) route low-priority classes to degraded bucket, 4) restart prom-adapter to flush backlog.
Jin K.: doing step 1 now: `kubectl scale deploy inference --replicas=20 -n inference` -> ok, replicas scaling. Watching queue.
OpsBot: autoscaler override applied by Jin K. (manual scale) :white_check_mark:
Sam L.: CPU on new pods is low but queue draining, latency dropping, errors down to ~6% after scaling.
Anya P.: start step 4 — restarting prom-adapter. `kubectl rollout restart deployment prom-adapter -n monitoring`
Maya R.: logs after restart show adapter reconnecting but spiking for some time. Observed a backlog of 45k metric points queued.
Priya S.: reason for backlog: recent deploy of a new model emitted high-cardinality labels per request (session_id) into a custom metric. Prometheus scrape size quadrupled and adapter queries to api-server are timing out. We need to drop that label or reduce label cardinality.
Sam L.: for immediate relief, patch prom-adapter to filter that metric. Applying configmap change now.
Jin K.: applied a temporary drop rule: filter out labels {session_id, request_id} from custom/inference_requests_total on the adapter side. Patch committed.
OpsBot: prom-adapter configmap updated by Jin K. (temporary cardinality filter) :hammer_and_wrench:
SupportBot: FYI support — customers A,C,D had increased error rates. Drafting message with status: degraded for some realtime chat flows; working on mitigation.
Maya R.: after the drop rule, adapter queries are back to normal latency (~200ms) and custom metric shows non-zero targets. HPA now sees metrics.
Sam L.: HPA status:
```
kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME             TARGETS    MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-hpa    75%/80%    3         50        18
```
Autoscaler kicked in to 18 replicas, expected to scale further if needed.
Anya P.: double-checking node pool capacity — cloud provider shows ephemeral shortage in gpu-us-west1-a zone. Spinning up a spare pool in us-west1-b (g4dn equivalent) as hot standby.
Jin K.: starting nodepool create; ETA ~6m. Meanwhile we might still be CPU-limited on current nodes due to many warmup tasks.
Sam L.: mitigation status: queue is draining but still above normal. Temporary rate limit for non-critical customers applied via gateway rules; this reduces incoming QPS by ~30%.
Priya S.: post-mitigation customer impact estimate: about 4 enterprise customers saw latency >2s for short windows; 3 customers saw request errors (retryable). No data loss. Support has initial blurb ready.
SupportBot: created incident ticket INC-2026-374; notifying customers with affected SLAs. Template: short summary + ETA for next update in 30m.
Maya R.: follow-up actions: 1) remove high-cardinality labels at source in model telemetry (deploy change), 2) add adapter-level reject/quotas for expensive queries, 3) improve HPA fallback when custom metrics unreachable (use CPU as fallback), 4) run load test to validate.
Sam L.: noted. Adding to postmortem list. Can someone take handoff for on-call overlap? My shift ends in 18m.
Jin K.: I can take on-call handoff. I'll continue watch and coordinate with cloud team for nodepool. Assigning to myself.
OpsBot: on-call handoff: Sam L. -> Jin K. (effective now) :loop:
Jin K.: I'll also open a short runbook PR for 'HPA metric pipeline lag' with steps we took and checklist for restarting adapter safely.
Anya P.: can we schedule an infra postmortem — propose 2h slot tomorrow with SRE, infra, runtime, and product devex to review telemetry emission and create enforcement on metric labels.
Sam L.: agreed. Also want a short-term probe to detect cardinality spikes: add alert when unique label count for custom/inference_requests_total > 5k/min.
Priya S.: noted. Customer impact summary for postmortem: ~15% error spike window lasted 18m, manual scale + adapter filters mitigated. No SLA breach yet but close for one enterprise — monitoring legal/CS follow-up.
SupportBot: next update to customers scheduled in 25m. Please add any customer-facing notes to INC-2026-374.
Jin K.: leaving watch for 60m then full handoff to oncall rotation. If nodepool creation fails, fallback is to route traffic to us-east1 with model-mirroring. Planning that if needed.
Sam L.: thanks all. Great quick coordination. We'll capture timelines in the postmortem. :heart:
IncidentBot: Incident resolved? Please update status when final.
